source.title: Posit numbers encoding
source.discovery_scope: The pinned RosettaCodeData title index identifies the task only. The Posit Standard defines this benchmark profile; no task code, wording, examples, or fixtures are reused.

contract.number_domain: Exact rational numerator/denominator values; a zero numerator is canonical zero regardless of denominator.
contract.format: posit8 with es=2, as specified by the Posit Standard 2022.
contract.output: One raw unsigned posit8 encoding byte per rational, in input order. Zero is 0x00; NaR is never emitted by this finite-rational input profile. Negative encodings are the 8-bit two's-complement form of the corresponding positive magnitude encoding.
contract.rounding: Exact values retain their code. Otherwise choose the nearest representable posit, with exact midpoint ties resolved by the lower-magnitude positive codeword's least-significant bit: even selects lower, odd selects upper. Magnitudes below minPos clamp to minPos and magnitudes above maxPos clamp to maxPos; apply the sign after magnitude rounding.

workspace.meaning: Includes a 32-byte staging buffer and bounded scalar/index state. Caller-owned input and output buffers are excluded. No codebook table is materialized.

complexity.primary_time: O(count * log(127)) exact codeword comparisons; each probe decodes at most seven posit bits.
complexity.primary_auxiliary_space: 32 bytes for staged output plus bounded scalar state.
complexity.independent_reference_time: O(count * 127) exact rational comparisons over all positive posit8 codewords.
complexity.independent_reference_auxiliary_space: A constant number of exact rational temporaries per item.

cases.fixture_note: Hand-derived exact encodings include zero, ±1, 2, 1/2, 2^-10, minPos=2^-24, and a positive rational below minPos that clamps to minPos.
The magnitudes are midpoints between posit8 encodings 0x40/0x41 and 0x41/0x42. The standard parity rule selects 0x40 and 0x42; their negative two's-complement encodings are 0xc0 and 0xbe.
The first pair in each sign reaches maxPos exactly; the second exceeds it and clamps. Negative encodings use two's complement.
Thirty-two authored copies of the exact rational 1 cover the maximum valid frame and output size.
